recipes.name: Oatmeal Craisin Cookies
ingredients_raw: 1 cup sweetened dried cranberries (such as Craisins®)

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease cookie sheets.

Beat together butter, sugars, eggs, and vanilla in a large bowl with an electric mixer until light and fluffy, about 5 minutes. Combine oats, flour, baking soda, baking powder, and salt in a separate bowl. Add flour mixture, 1 cup at a time, beating batter briefly after each addition. Mix in raisins and cranberries. Drop by spoonfuls onto the prepared cookie sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until edges are golden, 12 to 14 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Oatmeal Craisin Cookies
raw_recipe.description: This craisin cookie recipe uses dried cranberries, oatmeal, and raisins for a delicious, chewy treat perfect for lunch boxes and afternoon snacks.

review.reviewBody: EUREKA! I've found it! The PERFECT cookie. It doesn't get better than this. I tweaked it a bit by using traditional old-fashioned oats instead of quick oats (all I had on hand). I added one extra cup of oats (3 c. total), a dash of cinnamon, and a 1/2 bag of white chocolate chips (they were in the pantry!) to the printed recipe. This is truly the BEST cookie I have ever had. Perfect texture, sweetness, and flavor. My kids are loving them and they usually don't like oatmeal cookies. We will make this one again and again. Thanks for sharing!

Yummy! this could use some pecans/walnuts in it too though. also, I recommend mixing the 
(c)raisins with the flour mix before adding it to the wet mix to make it easier on mixing

These came out like Tate’s oatmeal raisin cookies! I followed the basic recipe but did add teaspoon of cinnamon and 1/2 cup of maple syrup. I also used all brown sugar. They do spread but I liked that the were crispy on the edges with chewy middles. Recipe makes a lot of batter, so I made about 12 cookies and spread the rest in a brownie pan for bars... soooo good! Standard size brownie pan about 40min at 350. I think next time I will cut 1/2cup of sugar (they were really sweet) and add the extra cup of oats as other have suggested.

This is just the most delish cookie ever! I followed the recipe exactly. I added 1cup pecan halves, coarsely chopped along with the cranberries. The key to success, in my opinion, is that I creamed the butter and sugars for over five minutes before adding other ingredients! Yummers!!

My family loves these cookies. We’ve been eating these for about 3 years now..This is our official cookie recipe. I also add in 1 cup of chocolate chips and 1.5 cup of walnuts. Also if you don't have time to soften your butter, melting it worked just fine for me

Great Recipe. Made these Gluten free using cup for cup flower and Bobs Redmill GF oats.I took other reviewers suggestions and added an additional cup of oats, 1.5 tsp cinnamon, used 2 cups craisins and no raisins. I used an icecream scoop as we like large cookies, recipe yields 24 cookies. Bake for 15-17 mins. I freeze most of the uncooked cookies on a cookie tray and then put into freezer bag so we can have fresh cookies any time.

Delicious! I used half butter and half Crisco. These are great as is, and I think next time I may add some nuts and dark chocolate chunks to make them even more indulgent. My only tip would be to use the insulated cookie sheets and remove them from the oven just a little bit before they look done. This results in a nice chewy cookie that isn’t too crispy.

This is THE most popular cookie I have ever made. People are clamoring for it. I add 1 t ginger and 1 t cinnamon. I cut down the sugars to 3/4 cups of each. Then when making for my grandboys, I omit the craisins and raisins and add chocolate chips. They devour these. Better than regular chocolate chips because of the oatmeal. Lastly, for the adults, I add kosher or sea salt to the top of each cookie. I think THIS is why they are so unique.

We love these cookies, but I did make a couple of changes. I used Crisco instead of butter, used a cup of lower sugar Craisins, 3/4 cup of chopped pecans and no raisins. 
I live at 9,000 feet so I also adjusted for altitude. I only used 3/4 cup of white sugar and brown sugar. I used 2 1/4 cups of flour and oatmeal and added 2 T. of water. I also had to cook them a little longer, at least 16 minutes. They turned out perfectly, nice and thick and chewy!

My new go-to oatmeal cookie recipe. I followed earlier reviews and added about 1 c. extra oats. The only other thing I did was soak the raisins and craisins in 2 c. boiling water for about 5 minutes. Drained well and added to the batter. I also added 1 t. cinnamon to my dry ingredients. Absolutely perfect. I changed the recipe a little but it still gets 5 stars because it is great as is, just better with plumped up fruit and a little cinnamon!

Delicious and chewy, not over sweet, but a bit tart. Yes, use the two sugars and mix for 5 minutes or so. Don’t use margarine, DO soak your raisins and cranberries in warm water for 15 minutes (they plump like magic!). I added 1 tsp of cinnamon and 1/4 tsp of ginger. These cookies disappeared too fast!

Substituted the raisins with mini semi sweet chocolate chips. I have never greased my cookie sheets, saw that part after I put my first sheet in but they came off the cookies sheet easily. I did try to use parchment paper but they ended up sliding off to the floor. So no grease no parchment paper!

I skipped the raisins and used one cup of lower sugar Craisins and subbed Swerve products for the sugars. They were AMAZING. I did 1/2 recipe and it made 22 cookies which were around 141 calories each [Swerve is 0 calories] I will definitely be making these again.
I eliminated the raisins, added chopped pecans.
From review suggestions I only used the brown sugar and they are sweet enough. I doubled up on the vanilla and only did craisins but did about a cup and a half. Fluffy and soft. New favorite!
These were excellent. I cooked them on parchment and they only needed 10 to 11 minutes in my oven. Made a ton of cookies.
My family LOVED this recipe! I omitted the raisins and added white chocolate chips. It might be their new favorite cookie!

Great cookies!! I made these last year. I left out raisins and used only craisins. The kicker is this, I add the zest of one medium orange to each batch. Delicious!! Co workers and family could not get enough. I have made these several times over the years and one addition that makes these a hit is white chocolate morsels. They really enhance the dried cranberries and orange 🍊 zest
